verses.text: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,
for gaining wisdom and discipline, for comprehending words of insight,
and for receiving instruction in wise living and in righteousness, justice, and equity.
To impart prudence to the simple and knowledge and discretion to the young,
let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel
by understanding the proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.
If they say, "Come along, let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush the innocent without cause,
let us swallow them alive like Sheol, and whole like those descending into the Pit.
We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.
Throw in your lot with us; let us all share one purse"—
my son, do not walk the road with them or set foot upon their path.
For their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed blood.
How futile it is to spread the net where any bird can see it!
But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors.
Wisdom calls out in the street, she lifts her voice in the square;
in the main concourse she cries aloud, at the city gates she makes her speech:
"How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?
If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you.
Because you refused my call, and no one took my outstretched hand,
because you neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction,
in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you,
when your dread comes like a storm, and your destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD.
They accepted none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.
So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
For the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil."

context.author: Solomon son of David, king of Israel, according to the heading (1:1). Chapters 1-9 are a father’s speeches to his son, with Wisdom speaking for herself, and many scholars think an editor set them at the front as the book’s introduction.
context.genre: Wisdom poetry: a father’s teaching and Lady Wisdom’s speeches
context.audience: A young man (“my son”) being trained for adult life in Israel, and with him “the simple” and the wise (1:4-5)
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: The book opens with its own title page: these are “the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel” (v.1), written so that the simple, the young and even the wise may grow in wisdom (vv.2-6). Its motto follows: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” (v.7). A father then warns his son not to join a gang that ambushes the innocent for loot (vv.8-19), and Wisdom herself stands in the streets and at the city gates, calling to anyone who will listen and warning those who refuse (vv.20-33).
context.custom: In Israel parents were the first teachers. The law told fathers to teach God’s words at home, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning (Deuteronomy 6:6-9), and Proverbs names the mother’s teaching alongside the father’s (v.8). The city gate was the public square of an ancient town, where elders sat, cases were judged and trade was done, so Wisdom speaks where everyone passes (v.21). A garland on the head and a pendant around the neck (v.9) were marks of honor.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 2 tells the son to search for wisdom like hidden treasure, and promises that it will guard him from evil men and from the adulteress.
context.timelineBible: Solomon reigned about 970-930 BC. 1 Kings 3 tells how he asked God for “an understanding heart” (1 Kings 3:9), and 1 Kings 4:32 says he spoke 3,000 proverbs. “The fear of the LORD” as the root of wisdom appears again in 9:10, Job 28:28 and Psalm 111:10.

translation.meaning: Skill for living. The same word is used for the skill of craftsmen (Exodus 31:3) and of sailors (Psalm 107:27). In Proverbs it is knowing how to live well before God and people.
Awe and reverence before God that shows itself in obedience. It is not terror but taking God seriously.
Open, naive, easily led. The simple are not yet fools but can be talked into anything (v.22; 14:15).

gospelParallels.note: Jesus speaks of “the wisdom of God” sending prophets, as Wisdom calls out here.
Jesus longs to gather Jerusalem’s children, who refused, as Wisdom called and was refused (vv.24-25).
Paul quotes the line about feet that run to shed blood (v.16; Isaiah 59:7).

otBackground.note: God gave Solomon wisdom; he spoke 3,000 proverbs.
Parents teach God’s words to their children.
“The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.”

overview.summary: The book states its purpose and its motto, the fear of the LORD, then a father warns his son against violent men and Wisdom calls out in the streets.
overview.settingLine: Wisdom calls at the city gates.

history.t: About 970-930 BC, a time of peace and trade.
Courts in Egypt and Israel trained young scribes.

customs.t: Elders judged and traded at the gate.
Signs of honor worn on head and neck.

archaeology.t: The ridge south of the Temple Mount was Solomon’s Jerusalem.
Egypt’s scribes also wrote a father’s teaching to his son, centuries before Solomon.

overview.discussion: Wisdom calls out in the busiest places, and the danger is not that she is hard to find but that people will not listen. Where am I hearing wisdom right now that I would rather not hear?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (1:1)

currentImage.caption: The Stepped Stone Structure on the east slope of the City of David, the oldest part of Jerusalem. Many archaeologists date it to the 10th or 9th century BC, the age of David and Solomon, though the dating is debated.
